title: Validate and restore retained operational work
description: Validate and restore a retained scope, including transfer into another environment; backup creation and migration interpretation are separate behaviors.
inputs: Selected retained backup and declared project identity
Authorized destination and expected destination state
preconditions: The requested scope and applicable action authority are explicit.
outputs: Validated restoration or transfer result with retained identities and declared scope
Explicit incompatibility, conflict, unavailable or interrupted outcome
behavior: With the original store unavailable and a valid complete backup accessible, restore reproduces the selected records, finding dispositions, subjects and revisions, decisions, provenance and required artifact content in the declared project scope.

Wrong-project input, unsupported interpretation, corrupted content or missing required artifacts is rejected before destination activation; source backup and unrelated destination content remain unchanged.

Restored reviews and verification results retain their original subject identities and applicability; neither restoration nor a different current engineering revision renews approval or evidence freshness.

An occupied or changed destination causes an explicit conflict unless a separately authorized safe replacement is supported; restoration never silently merges divergent histories or overwrites newer work.
An interrupted restoration exposes no partially restored state as complete or ready for resumption; retry identifies the actual destination state and preserves existing usable content.
When no usable backup exists, restoration reports unavailable and does not initialize an empty history as successful recovery.

A different project identity, divergent existing history or reused record identity with different content causes a conflict and leaves both histories intact; project-name similarity does not establish identity.
Excluded records or artifacts are visible before reliance, and the receiving result does not claim completeness outside the declared transferable scope.
Transfer leaves the source usable, does not change engineering-model files, and does not silently refresh assessments to the destination checkout revision.

failure_behavior.condition: Required source, interpretation or scope integrity cannot be established.
failure_behavior.outcome: Report the specific gap without claiming completeness, inventing decisions or mutating unrelated work.

failure_behavior.condition: Selected source or destination changes before a mutating operation can complete.
failure_behavior.outcome: Preserve established work and report conflict or interruption; no silent overwrite or automatic semantic merge.

unallocated_reason: The local operational-history extension is draft system analysis. Module/Interface and AR allocation are deferred to Architecture Allocation; existing v3 facets do not establish realization of this behavior.

sources.basis: Draft derivation from the refined IRs and RR proposal; no approval, implementation or satisfaction claim.
